name: highnoon-saloon-loop

footage.look: Keep the layered paper cut-out look exactly: cut-paper edges, flat paper shading, the same colours and the same lettering on every sign; no realism, no blur, no smoothing, no style change.
footage.physics: Physics: the building never moves and never changes size; the dust devils stay on the street strip at the bottom of the frame and never rise above the porch roof; there are exactly two dust devils and nothing else ever appears on the street, no plant, no cactus, no agave, no tumbleweed; the batwing doors swing on their hinges only; the round sign swings on its bracket only; nothing floats; the magenta backdrop never changes; every sign keeps its exact lettering.
footage.handoff: (loop: the last frame is the first frame)

notes: The High Noon paper saloon as a living site layer (Colby, 2026-09-09 16:30: 'animate this layer with some flickering lights and maybe dust devils passing and some other things, always beginning and ending on this frame'). The cabin recipe: the still as first AND last frame on Seedance 2.0, 480p probe, 10 s 1080p, closed with the loop tool (directional motion, so no ping-pong), keyed with the motion keyer (the sign sways, the doors swing), delivered as alpha WebM + HEVC MOV with previews.

render.prompt: Static camera, locked off, no push, no zoom, no pan, one continuous take from this one camera only; the frame never changes position, height or angle; no cut. Animate this exact paper-craft frontier saloon on its flat magenta plate as a gentle, continuous living loop. Light: the warm glow in every window, in the round window of the pediment and in the four hanging lanterns flickers unevenly like oil flame, visibly pulsing brighter and dimmer through the whole clip. Dust: a small dust devil, a spinning column of pale ochre dust, travels along the dusty street in front of the porch from the right edge of the frame to the left edge, never rising above the porch roof, and a second, smaller dust devil follows the same path near the end of the clip; the dust devils are translucent pale dust only, never solid objects; nothing else is ever added to the street: no plants, no cactus, no agave, no bushes, no tumbleweed, no animals, no people. Wind: the batwing saloon doors swing gently open and shut a few inches, the round wooden sign at the left end of the porch sways slightly on its bracket, the top corner of the WANTED poster lifts and settles, the lantern flames lean. The building, its roof, columns, balustrades, windows, barrels, crate, steps and the street stay exactly where they are. The ENTIRE backdrop stays one flat, uniform, solid magenta for the whole clip: no shadow, no gradient, no texture, no sky, nothing enters the magenta but the top of the swaying sign. The clip ends exactly as it began, on this same frame, so it loops naturally. Keep the layered paper cut-out look exactly: cut-paper edges, flat paper shading, the same colours and the same lettering on every sign; no realism, no blur, no smoothing, no style change. Physics: the building never moves and never changes size; the dust devils stay on the street strip at the bottom of the frame and never rise above the porch roof; there are exactly two dust devils and nothing else ever appears on the street, no plant, no cactus, no agave, no tumbleweed; the batwing doors swing on their hinges only; the round sign swings on its bracket only; nothing floats; the magenta backdrop never changes; every sign keeps its exact lettering. No text beyond the signs already there, no logos.
